courseOverview.title: Integrated STEM Curriculum Collection
courseOverview.description: A collection of phenomenon-based curricula spanning physics, earth science, and integrated STEM topics
courseOverview.framework: NGSS-aligned with emphasis on Science and Engineering Practices, Disciplinary Core Ideas, and Crosscutting Concepts

curricula.title: Energy Systems and Reliability: Learning from the Texas Blackouts
curricula.subject: Integrated STEM (Physics, Engineering, Social Studies)

centralPhenomenon.title: Texas Blackouts of February 2021
centralPhenomenon.description: Winter storm causing widespread power failures in Texas, revealing vulnerabilities in energy infrastructure
centralPhenomenon.realWorldRelevance: Community energy reliability and infrastructure resilience

parts.title: Understanding Energy Transfer and Circuits
parts.focus: Building foundational knowledge of electrical systems

parts.title: Energy Generation and Distribution
parts.focus: Exploring how electrical energy is produced and transmitted
keyPhenomena: Field interactions and energy transfer in wires
Grid system failures and disparate community impacts

parts.title: Designing Reliable Energy Systems
parts.focus: Creating solutions for sustainable and equitable energy access

curricula.metacognitiveBrief: Students develop systems thinking about energy infrastructure while learning core physics concepts of circuits, electromagnetic induction, and energy transfer. The curriculum emphasizes equity considerations and community decision-making processes.

curricula.title: Understanding Earth's Dynamic Systems: The Afar Region
curricula.subject: Earth Science

centralPhenomenon.title: Earthquake and crustal cracking in the Afar region (2005)
centralPhenomenon.description: Significant earthquake causing surface cracking in Ethiopian rift valley region
centralPhenomenon.realWorldRelevance: Understanding earthquake hazards and Earth's dynamic processes

parts.title: Forces and Earth System Stability
parts.focus: Understanding how forces create stability and change in Earth systems
keyPhenomena: Afar region earthquake and surface cracking
Global earthquake patterns and plate boundaries

parts.title: Earth's Interior and Energy Sources
parts.focus: Investigating how Earth's internal structure drives surface processes
keyPhenomena: Seismic wave data revealing Earth's layers
Note: Part II appears incomplete in source data

curricula.metacognitiveBrief: Students develop understanding of Earth as a dynamic system by investigating forces, matter, and energy interactions from particle scale to global scale. Emphasis on using multiple types of evidence to understand processes we cannot directly observe.

curricula.title: What can we do to make driving safer for everyone?
curricula.subject: Physics

centralPhenomenon.title: Puzzling patterns in traffic collision data
centralPhenomenon.description: While vehicle fatalities have decreased over decades, this trend has stalled and collisions/injuries are increasing
centralPhenomenon.realWorldRelevance: Vehicle safety design and community transportation safety

parts.title: What factors can make driving more risky?
parts.focus: Investigating distracted driving, reaction time, and momentum
keyPhenomena: Cart collisions with varying masses and velocities
Bus safety compared to other vehicles

parts.title: How can we make design decisions that will make driving safer?
parts.focus: Engineering design solutions for vehicle safety
keyPhenomena: Computer simulations of collision forces over time
Safety features effects on collision outcomes
Historical vs. modern safety design solutions

curricula.metacognitiveBrief: Students apply physics concepts of momentum and forces to real-world engineering design challenges. Strong emphasis on considering multiple stakeholders, tradeoffs, and community-specific factors in design solutions.

socialEmotionalConsiderations.traumaInformed: Vehicle collisions can be traumatic - requires consultation with school counselors and pre-unit communication with families
socialEmotionalConsiderations.equityFocus: Universal Design for Learning integration and socio-ecological framework for decision-making

curricula.title: How do we use radiation in our lives, and is it safe for humans?
curricula.subject: Physics

centralPhenomenon.title: Microwave ovens heating food and electronics storage
centralPhenomenon.description: People using microwave ovens to store electronics and how the oven heats food without an obvious heat source
centralPhenomenon.realWorldRelevance: Electromagnetic radiation safety and technology applications

parts.title: How does a microwave oven heat up food?
parts.focus: Investigating wave properties and electromagnetic energy transfer

parts.title: How do we use electromagnetic radiation safely in our lives?
parts.focus: Exploring the electromagnetic spectrum and radiation safety

crosscuttingConcepts: Cause and Effect: Mechanism and Explanation
Energy and Matter: Flows, Cycles, and Conservation
curricula.metacognitiveBrief: Students develop sophisticated understanding of electromagnetic radiation through both wave and particle models, learning to evaluate scientific claims about radiation safety using evidence-based reasoning.

safetyConsiderations.radiationSensitivity: Recognition that EM radiation topics can cause student anxiety
safetyConsiderations.traumaInformed: Open communication about radiation concerns with emotional support

overarchingThemes.phenomenaDriven: All curricula use authentic, puzzling phenomena to drive student questions and learning
overarchingThemes.threeDimensionalLearning: Integration of Science and Engineering Practices, Disciplinary Core Ideas, and Crosscutting Concepts
overarchingThemes.realWorldRelevance: Strong connections to community issues, current events, and personal relevance
overarchingThemes.equityAndInclusion: Universal Design for Learning, trauma-informed approaches, and consideration of diverse perspectives
overarchingThemes.systemsThinking: Emphasis on understanding complex systems and interactions across scales

commonPractices.modelingProgression: Students develop increasingly sophisticated models throughout each curriculum
commonPractices.dataAnalysis: Extensive use of authentic data from real-world sources
commonPractices.engineeringDesign: Integration of engineering design process with scientific investigation
commonPractices.argumentation: Students construct evidence-based arguments and evaluate claims
commonPractices.mathematicalThinking: Application of mathematics to understand and predict phenomena

commonCrosscuttingConcepts.energyAndMatter: Central to energy systems, Earth processes, collision physics, and electromagnetic radiation
commonCrosscuttingConcepts.systemsAndModels: Used across all curricula to understand complex interactions
commonCrosscuttingConcepts.causeAndEffect: Emphasis on mechanistic thinking and evidence-based explanations
commonCrosscuttingConcepts.stabilityAndChange: Understanding how systems maintain stability and undergo change
commonCrosscuttingConcepts.scaleAndProportion: Connections across scales from particle to global levels

formativeAssessment: Transfer tasks applying learning to new contexts

implementationConsiderations.timeRequirements: Curricula range from 14 lessons to 27+ days, requiring significant time investment
implementationConsiderations.materialNeeds: Mix of low-cost materials, simulations, and authentic data sources
implementationConsiderations.teacherPreparation: Requires comfort with three-dimensional instruction and phenomenon-based teaching
implementationConsiderations.studentPrerequisites: Building on prior learning while accessible to diverse learners
implementationConsiderations.communityConnections: Opportunities for local partnerships and community engagement
